messages.author: 753bdf02bbd6d099
messages.subject: Define maximum distance between clusters
parts:
Hi all,

I'm very new to the secr package, so please forgive my inexperience. I'm planning on running hundreds of simulations to assess different trap layouts. One of these trap layouts will be a cluster design. I've managed to figure out the code to randomly define cluster layouts for each iteration, but I don't seem to be able to specify a maximum distance between clusters. Is this even possible to do? Below is an example of my what I've figured out so far:

cluster <- make.grid(nx = 2, ny = 2, 
                     spacing  = 500, 
                     detector ='proximity')

tempgrid <- trap.builder (n = 9, cluster,
                          region = cbind(x = c(0,31623,31623,0),
                                         y = c(0,0,31623,31623)),
                          rotation = "-", 
                          edgemethod = "allinside", 
                          samplefactor = 2,
                          plt = TRUE)


So I want clusters to comprise 4 stations (2 x 2), spaced 500m from one another. I then build the trap layout by specifying how many clusters I want (n = 9) across a ~1000 sq km area (region). This same region needs to be used for all other simulations using different trap layouts (e.g., block design, strip design, etc.). Lastly, I want the rotation to be random and for all clusters to fall within "region". The only issue is, when I run this code the clusters are placed across the entire "region" (I understand why this is the case, since that's the region I've specified), but is there a way to limit cluster placement so that clusters are never more than 5km (for example) from one another? It would also be great to be able to specify a minimum distance too; for instance, clusters can't be closer than 1km from one another.

I guess I could somehow specify a second, smaller region, within the first region, to which I distribute the clusters. But I'm not sure if that's the best way to go, nor do I know how to attempt that?

I hope all of this makes sense? I'd really appreciate some help on this.

Thanks in advance!

Ross

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Define maximum distance between clusters
parts:
Hi Ross

I think you have reached the limit of what is possible with secr 2.10. Buried in the code for trap.builder there is a note suggesting that future versions should allow a minimum separation, so I guess it's not yet available! Apart from that, I tend to think what you are attempting is rather arcane and likely to result in very slight differences in estimator efficiency. Specifically, the properties of the SECR estimates can probably be determined with a systematic grid of widely-spaced clusters, and cluster rotation probably is not relevant if animals are placed at random. Also, you are aiming to constrain a SRS (simple random sample), but a spatially balanced sample would be better (systematic, GRTS or the recently published Balanced Acceptance Sampling - see package SDraw).

Your solution - containing random clusters within a smaller region to adjust (average) spacing - might work, but is it worth the hassle?

Murray

PS You have rotation = "-", but I think the idea is to use a negative number: rotation = -1.
